The server received the request headers; the client should send the body.
What to do: Normally invisible. Only relevant when you use "Expect: 100-continue".
The server agrees to switch protocols, for example to WebSocket.
What to do: If a WebSocket fails to open, check the Upgrade and Connection headers through any proxy.
WebDAV: the server has accepted the request and is still working on it.
What to do: Rare; treat as "wait".
Lets the browser preload resources while the server prepares the final response.
What to do: Used with Link headers for faster page loads.
What to do: For GET the body contains the resource; for POST the result of the action.
The request succeeded and created a new resource.
What to do: Look for a Location header with the new resource's URL.
The request was accepted for processing, but the work is not finished.
What to do: Poll the status URL the API gives you.
The response was modified by a proxy.
What to do: Typical for DELETE and for PUT without a result. Do not try to parse JSON.
Success; the client should reset the form or view.
The server returns only the byte range requested.
What to do: Used for video streaming and resumable downloads (Range header).
What to do: Rare; pick one of the links offered.
The resource has a new permanent URL.
What to do: Update links and bookmarks. Search engines transfer ranking to the new URL.
What to do: Keep using the original URL; browsers may change POST to GET.
Redirects to another URL with GET after a POST.
What to do: The classic post/redirect/get pattern.
The cached version is still valid.
What to do: Not an error: the browser uses its cache (ETag or Last-Modified matched).
Temporary redirect that keeps the HTTP method.
What to do: Like 302 but POST stays POST.
Permanent redirect that keeps the HTTP method.
What to do: Like 301 but POST stays POST.
The server cannot understand the request because of a client error.
What to do: Check the JSON syntax, required fields, URL encoding and header sizes.
Authentication is required or has failed.
What to do: Send valid credentials or a fresh token. Check the Authorization header.
What to do: Some APIs use it when a plan limit or payment is missing.
You are authenticated but not allowed to access this.
What to do: Check permissions, IP allow lists, CORS and firewall (WAF) rules.
The resource does not exist at this URL.
What to do: Check the URL for typos, trailing slashes and case; the resource may have been removed.
The HTTP method is not supported for this URL.
What to do: Look at the Allow header; you may need POST instead of GET.
The server cannot produce a response matching the Accept headers.
What to do: Relax the Accept header.
What to do: Configure proxy credentials.
The server timed out waiting for the request.
What to do: Retry; check slow networks and large uploads.
The request conflicts with the current state of the resource.
What to do: Typical for edit conflicts and duplicate entries. Refresh and retry.
What to do: Remove links; search engines drop the page faster than for 404.
What to do: Add it or send with a body the client can measure.
A condition in the request headers failed (If-Match etc.).
What to do: The resource changed; fetch the latest version.
The request body is larger than the server allows.
What to do: Reduce the upload or raise client_max_body_size / the limit.
The URL is longer than the server accepts.
What to do: Use POST with a body instead of a long query string.
The server does not support the request's content type.
What to do: Set the correct Content-Type, e.g. application/json.
The requested byte range is outside the resource.
What to do: Check the Range header against the file size.
The Expect header cannot be met.
What to do: Some servers use it to reject bots.
The request was sent to a server that cannot answer it.
What to do: Typical with HTTP/2 connection reuse and wrong TLS host.
The syntax is right but the content failed validation.
What to do: Read the error body for field-level messages.
What to do: Wait or unlock.
The server will not process a request that might be replayed.
What to do: Retry after the handshake.
The client must switch to another protocol.
What to do: Use HTTPS or a newer HTTP version.
The server requires a conditional request.
What to do: Slow down and respect the Retry-After header; add exponential back-off.
The headers (often cookies) are too big.
What to do: Clear cookies or reduce header size.
The content is blocked for legal reasons.
What to do: Not fixable on the client side.
The server hit an unexpected condition.
What to do: A bug or misconfiguration on the server; check the server logs.
The server does not support the requested functionality.
What to do: The method or feature is not available.
A gateway or proxy received an invalid response from the upstream server.
What to do: The application behind the proxy crashed or is unreachable; check upstream health and timeouts.
The server is temporarily unable to handle the request.
What to do: Overload or maintenance; retry later and honour Retry-After.
The gateway did not get a timely response from the upstream server.
What to do: Increase proxy timeouts or speed up the backend.
The HTTP version is not supported.
The server cannot store the representation (WebDAV).
What to do: Free up disk space.
The server detected an infinite loop (WebDAV).
What to do: Check redirects or links.
You must authenticate to access the network.
What to do: Typical for captive portals (hotel Wi-Fi); open a browser and log in.
